resources.string: Slide your paddle, add spin and outlast the other edges. Up to four on one screen.
Duel the computer. Add more computers to fill the other edges.
Two to four people on one screen, each with a thumb on their own edge.
First to a number of points, or last paddle standing with lives. With three or four players, lives work best.
A wide paddle, a slow ball or extra balls appear on the court. The last player to touch the ball gets the prize.
A slower ball, wider paddles and a longer countdown, for players who find fast games hard.
Drag with a thumb (arrow buttons work too), or use one switch: the paddle follows the ball by itself and the switch changes your return angle.
Turn each player\'s labels toward their own edge. Switch off to keep everything upright.
Everybody picks in secret, then the hands are revealed together.
Outguess the computer. Add more computers for a bigger showdown.
Two to four people on one screen. Everyone picks on their own side and nobody can peek.
Classic is rock, paper and scissors. Lizard-Spock adds two more moves, so ties are rarer.
Best of 3, 5 or 7 rounds, or Elimination: the losers of each round drop out and the last player standing wins. Ties replay.
How long players have to lock in a move. When time runs out a random move is picked.
No time pressure: a doubled pick timer, a slower countdown, and the result stays until someone taps Next round.
